meta.title: DALgo — database abstraction layer for Go and TypeScript
meta.description: DALgo is a database abstraction layer for Go and TypeScript. One interface, many databases — in-memory, SQL, Firestore, files, inGitDB, OpenVaultDB. The Go module is the main implementation; the TypeScript package @dalgo/core is on npm.
meta.og_title: DALgo — database abstraction layer for Go and TypeScript
meta.og_description: One interface. Many databases. Write storage-agnostic Go and TypeScript.
hero.eyebrow: Open source · Go module · TypeScript package
hero.lede: DALgo is a database abstraction layer for Go and TypeScript. Write your domain logic once against a single, well-tested interface — swap Postgres for Firestore, an in-memory store for a real one — without touching your business code. The Go module is the main implementation; the TypeScript package, @dalgo/core, is published on npm.
diagram.figure_label: DALgo bridges your Go code to many databases
diagram.canvas_label: Graph: your Go code talks to DALgo, which adapts to SQL (SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL), local storage (in-memory, file system, inGitDB), OpenVaultDB, Firestore and HTTP sources, or to your own custom adapter.
diagram.fallback: Your code → DALgo → SQL (SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL) · in-memory, file system, inGitDB · OpenVaultDB · Firestore · HTTP sources · or your own custom adapter.
why.title: Storage is a detail, not a destiny.
why.kicker: Six reasons developers reach for DALgo on day one. The longer case is Why use DALgo, and the limits are in When to use DALgo, and when not to.
why.1.title: Storage-agnostic logic
why.1.text: Write business code against dal.DB. Decide later whether it lives in Postgres, Firestore, or a JSON file on disk.
why.2.title: Less code, more readable
why.2.text: One small, opinionated API replaces piles of driver-specific boilerplate. Records, keys, queries, transactions — uniform across every adapter.
why.3.title: Testable by construction
why.3.text: Swap a production driver for the built-in dalgo2memory adapter in tests. Need mocks instead? The generated mocks package ships in the core repo.
why.4.title: Hooks & logging, for free
why.4.text: Because every operation goes through one interface, observability and audit logging are a wrapper — not a refactor.
why.5.title: One end-to-end test suite
why.5.text: Ten Go adapters pass the same shared conformance suite in CI. Conformance is the contract; the others are listed below with what they do and do not support.
why.6.title: Transactions, the Go way
why.6.text: Read-only and read-write transactions are first-class. Pass a closure, get atomicity — without leaking driver-specific transaction types into your domain.
adapters.title: Same interface. Different stores.
adapters.kicker: Two adapters ship inside the core module. Ten Go adapters pass the shared conformance suite; the rest are listed below with their limits.
companion.title: Companion modules
companion.mocks: — generated mocks for every DALgo interface, now part of the core repo (the standalone mocks4dalgo repo is archived).
companion.e2e: — the shared conformance suite (dalgotest.RunConformance) that the adapters above run against, now part of the core repo (the standalone dalgo-end2end-tests repo is archived).
companion.demo: — see how little code you need to ship a working app.
companion.auth: — opinionated record structs for user-auth tables.
companion.memcache: — App Engine memcache wrapper for DALgo transactions.
qs.title: Install the core. Pick an adapter. Write a record.
qs.kicker: A working example in fewer than 40 lines.
qs.step1: Install the core module. The built-in dalgo2memory adapter ships with it — no extra dependency to get started.
qs.step2: Open a database. The returned dal.DB is the only type your app needs to know about.
qs.step3: Define a record, set its data, then read it back by key.
qs.step4: Later, swap dalgo2memory for dalgo2sqlite or dalgo2firestore. Your handlers don't change.
col.title: Less ceremony for everyday CRUD.
col.kicker: A generic, session-less dal.Collection[T] handle returns typed values directly — no key wrangling, no record wrapping, no type assertions. It is additive over the core API and works with every Go adapter.
col.more: The same handle also offers Insert (generated id), InsertWithID, All, First, Count, Exists, Update, Delete, batch InsertMany, and In(parentKey) for nested collections.
col.cmp_kicker: The same operations written against the standard library and against DALgo. The DALgo version is backend-agnostic — identical code runs on Firestore, SQL, the filesystem, or the in-memory adapter.
col.get_lead: Read one user by id — and return a typed value directly.
col.ban_lead: In one transaction: load the user; if not banned, flag them and add a Ban record.
if.title: Small enough to memorize.
if.kicker: Strict enough to keep every adapter honest.
if.prose: Every DALgo adapter — SQL, NoSQL, embedded, filesystem — implements the same dal.DB contract. Read operations live on ReadSession; mutating operations live on ReadwriteSession. Transactions are closures: pass a function, the driver gives you a session, your code never sees a driver-specific handle.
if.flash: Drivers that can't implement an operation return dal.ErrNotSupported — explicit failure beats silent nonsense.
q.title: More than get and set.
q.kicker: A structured query builder, hierarchical collections, and schema-aware key mapping — capability-based across adapters.
q.prose: DALgo ships a structured query builder for the common database reads: filters, ordering, LIMIT, column projection, GROUP BY / HAVING, aggregates like COUNT(*) and SUM, and inner / left equi-joins. Keys can model nested document paths such as countries/ireland/cities/dublin, and a parent key scopes a query to a nested collection.
q.flash: Adapter support is capability-based: a backend that can't run a query feature returns dal.ErrNotSupported, so tests share one query shape and skip cleanly. The serialized query format lives in TugQL.
dt.title: Used in DataTug development
dt.text: DataTug helps developers explore database schemas, write and run queries, and understand their results. DALgo provides a data-access seam in DataTug’s development ecosystem. Read how DataTug’s development tools were built.
close.title: Storage is a detail. Treat it like one.
close.text: DALgo is MIT-licensed and waiting for you to break it. The Go module is production-tested; the TypeScript package is at 0.x. Contributions for new adapters and edge cases are welcome.

ts.title: The same idea in TypeScript.
ts.kicker: @dalgo/core is the browser-neutral TypeScript implementation: hierarchical keys, typed collections, structured queries and transaction-only writes.
ts.prose: Install it from npm with npm install @dalgo/core. The package has no database SDK of its own and does not connect to a database by itself; an adapter does. Source: dal-go/dalgo-js.
ts.adapters: The TypeScript adapters live in dal-go/dalgo-http-adapters. Seven are published on npm: @dalgo/firestore (the reference adapter), @dalgo/indexeddb, @dalgo/ovdb, @dalgo/bigquery, @dalgo/d1, @dalgo/http and @dalgo/sqlite-wasm. More are in development and not yet on npm.
ts.flash: Maturity: @dalgo/core is at 0.x, and several adapters are read-only or query-only. Each adapter's README states what it supports; an operation it cannot do fails explicitly.

dalgo2memory.desc: In-memory adapter shipped in the core module — the default store for tests, examples, and local development. Runs most structured-query features end to end.

dalgo2fs.desc: Built-in adapter mapping the OS file system to DALgo records — handy for demos and simple local persistence.

dalgo2sql.desc: Adapter for the standard database/sql — any compliant driver.

dalgo2sqlite.desc: SQLite-specific driver: schema, DDL, concurrency-aware operations on top of dalgo2sql.

dalgo2postgres.desc: PostgreSQL-specific driver on top of dalgo2sql: forces the postgres dialect, introspects catalogs and applies Postgres DDL.

dalgo2mysql.desc: MySQL-specific driver on top of dalgo2sql: schema introspection and MySQL DDL. CI runs the conformance suite against MySQL 8.

dalgo2ingitdb.desc: Adapter for inGitDB — a Git-native database with branchable, mergeable data. Reads and writes; a transaction is a Git commit. Lives in the inGitDB organization.

dalgo2openvaultdb.desc: Adapter for OpenVaultDB through its ovdb serve HTTP API: reads and transactional writes.

dalgo2firestore.desc: For Google Cloud Firestore — a globally distributed NoSQL document database.

dalgo2http.desc: Declarative HTTP endpoints — JSON, plus named XML and CSV resources — exposed as DALgo collections. Read-only by design.

adapters_more.dalgo2mssql: SQL Server, no structured-query compiler yet
adapters_more.dalgo2duckdb: DuckDB, no schema introspection or DDL yet
adapters_more.dalgo2namecheap: Namecheap domains and DNS, reads and writes
